card.title: RESISTANCE COUNCIL
card.text: Pin target unit. Deal 1 damage to the enemy HQ. Add a RESISTANCE card to the enemy deck.
card.flavorText: Created by Jean Moulin at the request of General de Gaulle, the National Council of the Resistance (French: Conseil National de la Résistance, or CNR) was the body that unified the various French Resistance movements under German occupation, encompassing all political tendencies. It met for the first time on May 27, 1943, in Paris, bringing together around the same table representatives of the eight major resistance movements, the two most important pre-war trade unions, and the six main political parties of the French Third Republic. The primary mission of the CNR was to put an end to the fragmentation and rivalries that could weaken the Resistance from within. It became the sole and legitimate interlocutor for General de Gaulle's Free France, based in London. The Council coordinated intelligence, the clandestine press, sabotage actions, and the armed struggle across the entire country. In March 1944, the CNR adopted a fundamental document: its programme. This document did not only plan for the national insurrection at the time of the D-Day landings. It also outlined the "Jours Heureux" (happy days), a project of economic and social reforms for post-war France, including social security and nationalizations, which durably marked the country's reconstruction. The unifying action of the CNR allowed for the integration of the French Forces of the Interior into the regular army during the Liberation. Its legacy, both military and political, enabled France to take its place among the victors and regain its full sovereignty.
